To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the planning form had a positive effect on the performance of students who were of medium + low self-competence, but not on the performance of those of high self-competence and (2) the planning form did not have a positive effect on performance for any students who had high perceived self-competences.

(1) planning is an effective self-regulatory strategy for enhancing performance; (2) planning is more effective for students of lower self-competence; and (3) planning is more beneficial when the task is unfamiliar and complex.

(1) the use of planning forms was positively associated with the self-regulated writing performance of teacher education majors; and, (2) this positive association was found only among those students who perceived themselves to be of average or low ability to write.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the self-regulatory processes involved in student planning, and the effect of planning on student performance.
the effects of self-regulated planning on the performance of students of differing self-perceptions of competence.
the effect of planning on the self-regulated behavior of college students.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effect of the planning form on student performance depended on the student's self-perceived capability.
planning and perceived self-competent students are more likely to self-regulate their performance.
planning is a strategy that can enhance self-motivated performance, particularly for individuals with low or medium + low perceived competence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of planning forms is a viable strategy for increasing self-motivation in the classroom.
the use of self-regulated planning strategies is a viable method for improving the self-motivated performance of college students of average or lower perceived self-competency.
the planning form helped students of low + medium self-competence to improve performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
students with low perceived competence may benefit from being given forms to help them plan and organize their work.
the effect of student planning and self-competence on self-regulated performance may be mediated by the student’s perception of their own ability to perform the task.
planning can be a useful strategy for students who lack confidence in their own abilities.
